evidence: src/domain/services/StockManager.ts: class StockManager exposes canReserveStock, reserveStock and releaseStock. All three are stock-reservation operations over Order.lines.
canReserveStock delegates to product.canReserve(line.quantity), so the availability rule stays in the Product entity.
reserveStock calls product.reserve(line.quantity) and releaseStock calls product.release(line.quantity). Neither changes stock state directly, so they don't bypass the entity.
Minor: the lookup products.find(p => p.id === line.productId) is repeated in all three methods. Missing products are rejected in canReserveStock but silently skipped in reserveStock and releaseStock.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, src/domain/services/StockManager.ts, and it covers a single concern: reserving and releasing stock across the lines of an order. The service doesn't re-implement the stock invariant. Each method calls the Product entity's own abstractions (canReserve, reserve, release), so the availability rule stays in Product and is not copied into the service. The same product lookup (products.find(p => p.id === line.productId)) appears in all three methods. That is repeated code, not a duplicated business rule. One small inconsistency: canReserveStock treats a missing product as a failure, while reserveStock and releaseStock silently skip it. This doesn't split the module's concern or bypass its abstractions.
